props.role_shape: A caseload of around 25 patients in their own homes, worked mostly alone, with a weekly MDT as the only routine point of contact with colleagues.
props.register: Plain and clinical. This is a provider that would rather hear how you decided than how confident you felt.
props.what_stage_one_tests: Whether you are comfortable holding a decision on your own, and whether you can say when you would escalate.

props.intro: Four things the brief keeps returning to. Two of them are about working alone; the third is about what you write down afterwards.

props.prompt: A visit where you made a clinical call on your own and had to decide whether to escalate.
skeleton: The setting, and who else was involved
What you noticed that made this a decision rather than a routine visit
What you weighed before you acted
What you did, and when you escalated or chose not to
What you wrote up, and when

props.prompt: A wound you assessed and managed independently over several visits.
skeleton: The regime you chose and why
What you changed when it did not respond
How you knew it was working

props.intro: Who you are likely to meet, and what each of them is listening for.

panel.what_they_probe: Whether you can hold your nerve alone in someone's house.
Careful record-keeping — they sit in on the second stage.

props.prompt: A time your notes were the thing the next clinician had to work from.
skeleton: What the next person did with it

props.format: Panel, including a scenario drawn from a real case on the caseload.
props.bring: NMC PIN, driving licence, and the dates of your community roles.
props.note: The brief does not say how long the second stage runs. Ask when you confirm.

props.intro: Two things this brief suggests they will want to test before they offer.

concerns.concern: You came out of an acute ward, and the two people they hired before you found the autonomy hard.
concerns.evidence_quote: Community Staff Nurse — Weald Valley Community Trust, 2022–2026

concerns.concern: The caseload includes IV therapy in the community, and your CV does not mention it.

props.intro: A few worth having in your pocket. Ask the ones you actually want answered.
questions: What did the two hires who found the autonomy hard say they were missing?
How is the caseload split across the Crawley corridor, and how often does it move?
Who is on the end of the phone when a visit turns into a decision?

competencies.label: Working autonomously on a rural caseload
competencies.source_quote: Comfortable lone working with a rural caseload

competencies.label: Independent wound assessment and management
competencies.source_quote: at least one of them in a community or district nursing setting

competencies.label: Same-day documentation others rely on
competencies.source_quote: the postholder must document every visit before the end of the day
competencies.failed_quote: the postholder must document every visit before the end of the day

questions.text: Tell me about the last clinical decision you made with nobody available to check it.
How do you decide, in someone's home, that a situation needs escalating now rather than at the end of the round?
Two people we hired from acute wards found the autonomy hard. What makes you different?
Walk me through how you assess a wound you are seeing for the first time.
Describe a wound that did not respond to the regime you chose. What did you change?
How would you get up to speed on IV therapy in the community?
What goes into your write-up of a visit, and when do you do it?
A colleague picks up your caseload tomorrow. What would they struggle to find in your notes?
